metadata.case_name: CHUNG YIU KWAN v. EAGLE ENGINEERING CO

plaintiff.occupation_before: driver and fitter of air-conditioning and metal kitchen equipment units
plaintiff.education_level: educated up to Form 3 secondary school

source: There was a 7cm laceration over the left shoulder, and a 10cm laceration over the lateral aspect of the left calf.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of shoulder or upper arm

injuries.description: 10cm laceration over the lateral aspect of the left calf
source: There was a 7cm laceration over the left shoulder, and a 10cm laceration over the lateral aspect of the left calf.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of lower leg

injuries.description: Muscle wastage of left leg (1/2 cm) compared to right
source: Dr David Lee examined the plaintiff in August 1994. He found muscle wastage of 1/2 cm on the left leg compared to the right.
Dr Chan also found evidence of muscle wasting in the injured leg.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at lower leg level

injuries.description: Loss of mobility in left leg
source: there has been loss of mobility in his left leg.

injuries.description: Recurrent sprain of back due to compensating for left leg weakness
source: His attempts at compensating for that weakness in turn caused him to sprain his back on many occasions.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: Unsightly scars on his shoulder and left calf
Muscle wastage of 1/2 cm on the left leg compared to the right
Left leg remained very weak and unable to bear much weight
Severe pain at his left ankle whenever he carried any heavy object
Unable to run nor to crouch down
Sprained his back on many occasions
Curtailment of participation in soccer and other sports
Affected ability to lift heavy objects
Felt embarrassed by the unsightly scar on his left shoulder because it resembled a chop wound

treatments_received: follow up treatment at Sai Ying Pun Clinic
attended the Tuen Mun Hospital about five times

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Curtailment of participation in basketball, table tennis, badminton and especially soccer; estimated deprivation period approximately 12 years from date of accident
Embarrassment and social consequence from 'unsightly scar on his left shoulder because it resembled a chop wound, leading others to think that he had been injured in a gang fight.'
Left leg weakness and inability to bear weight on left side; affected ability to lift heavy objects
Loss of mobility in left leg; inability to run or crouch
